title: the Deep Rising Revisited
premise: Sable Ravensworth smuggles stolen memories through the orbital customs of Meridian Colony while quietly maintaining a beacon whose origin no one can explain. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream—a voice counting down from the relay at the edge of dead space—Sable realizes the beacon she tends is transmitting, and that her own fragmented memories may be its message. Pursued by customs enforcers who want the signal silenced and haunted by the truth that she was engineered, not born, Sable races to reach the relay before the countdown ends. She arrives as the signal completes: the beacon was built by her original self, a lost scout who seeded copies of her memories into the colony's water supply, and the children's dream is a rescue call across decades. Choosing loyalty to the colony over the law that made her invisible, Sable broadcasts the full archive of what happened to the dead scout fleet—and finally becomes someone with a name worth remembering.
about_author: Marguerite Villalobos is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent nine years maintaining automated beacons along the Pacific coast before turning to fiction. Her work explores the loneliness of infrastructure and the people who keep it alive.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A routine smuggling run past orbital customs, hiding contraband memories in her own neural lace, followed by her quiet ritual of servicing the unregistered beacon on the colony's far ridge. Establishes her invisibility as survival. Emotional beat: competent solitude shading into unease when the beacon logs show activity she didn't cause.

chapters.title: Contraband in the Blood
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She delivers a client's purchased memories—a dead husband's last morning—to a grieving widow, witnessing how memory shapes identity. Customs officer Dario Voss nearly catches her, hinting he suspects more than cargo. Emotional beat: tenderness for clients versus fear of exposure; first spark of Voss's obsession.

chapters.title: Children Who Dream in Unison
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Market gossip turns strange: forty children report the same dream—a voice counting down from somewhere cold. Sable recognizes the relay coordinates from her beacon's maintenance codes. Emotional beat: dread crystallizing into purpose; she realizes the dream originates from her own silent charge.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Dario Voss's POV. Voss traces memory-trafficking patterns and finds they orbit around one unremarkable freight runner. He pulls the colony's founding records and discovers the beacon predates the colony itself. Emotional beat: righteous certainty curdling into fascination; Voss begins wanting the truth more than the arrest.

chapters.title: What the Water Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Analyzing the children's dream fragments, Sable finds embedded data—images of a scout fleet, faces she somehow knows. She tests her own water ration and detects trace nanite residue. Emotional beat: vertigo; the horrifying suspicion that the memories inside her were placed there.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Code
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She seeks out her fence, old Iyo Tanaka, who reveals the beacon's commissioning fee was paid sixty years ago by the Deep Rising scout program—with a name attached: Ravensworth. Emotional beat: shaken loyalty; Iyo warns her that some cargoes are better left undelivered.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss interrogates a retired customs clerk who processed the scout fleet's final departure, learning the fleet never transmitted home and was declared lost to save face. Emotional beat: disillusionment with the institution he serves; justice and procedure visibly diverging.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Classroom
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The children's countdown accelerates; one girl, Wren, draws the relay's interior in perfect detail—including a door only someone standing inside would know. Sable realizes the signal isn't just broadcasting; it's teaching them. Emotional beat: protective fury; these children are being conscripted as receivers.

chapters.title: Seizure Order
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Command orders the beacon destroyed and all dreaming children quarantined for 'memory hygiene.' Voss volunteers to lead the raid, planning privately to reach the beacon first. Emotional beat: betrayal of his own badge; he now believes the colony is being lied to at scale.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Warned by Iyo, Sable flees with Wren, who has become the strongest receiver, aboard her patched freighter. They burn toward dead space ahead of the enforcement squadron. Emotional bond between smuggler and child deepens. Emotional beat: fugitive terror transmuted into fierce guardianship.

chapters.title: The Archive in Her Head
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Under relay-proximity interference, Sable's suppressed memories unlock: she is a copy—a backup consciousness printed into a body grown from the lost scout Sable Ravensworth, launched as a living failsafe. Emotional beat: identity collapse; everything she called herself was scaffolding.

chapters.title: Wren's Dream, Whole
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Inside the shared dream, Wren walks the scout ship Deep Rising and meets the original Sable's recorded presence, who asks the children not to save her but to remember the crew. Emotional beat: grief transformed into mission; the children understand they are witnesses, not victims.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The freighter crosses into the relay's silence zone where no signal can escape except through the beacon itself. Voss's ship shadows them, weapons hot but holding. Emotional beat: claustrophobic stillness; two enemies drifting toward the same truth.

chapters.title: Boarding the Relay
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable docks and enters the ancient relay, finding the original crew's remains and the beacon's core: a message sixty years in the buffering, addressed to whoever carries her memories. Emotional beat: awe and mourning; she stands inside her own origin.

chapters.title: Voss at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss boards alone against orders, weapon drawn, demanding Sable surrender the archive. She shows him the crew's final logs—the fleet found something that killed them, and command knew. Emotional beat: standoff dissolving; Voss lowers his gun and chooses the truth over the law.

chapters.title: The Message Completes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The countdown reaches zero and the beacon transmits the full Deep Rising archive—not a distress call but testimony, aimed at every receiver the nanites touched. Command scrambles to jam it. Emotional beat: triumphant urgency; the signal is loose and cannot be recalled.

chapters.title: Jamming the Sky
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Back at the colony, command moves to purge the children's nanites and erase the transmission record. Voss defects openly, feeding Sable the jamming schedule. Emotional beat: costly allegiance; Voss trades his career, maybe his freedom, for the story to survive.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Using the relay's full array and Wren coordinating the children as a distributed antenna, Sable rebroadcasts the archive on civilian bands, unstoppable by any single authority. Emotional beat: collective catharsis; the colony hears its own buried history in the voices of its children.

chapters.title: Reckoning at Customs House
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Command falls as colonists demand answers; Voss testifies to the cover-up, accepting arrest as the price. The children are released from quarantine. Emotional beat: justice achieved outside the law, paid for inside it; bittersweet vindication.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Woman
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable returns to the beacon and formally registers it—and herself—in the colony rolls under both names: the smuggler's alias and the scout's true name. Emotional beat: integration; she stops choosing between the woman she was made from and the woman she became.

chapters.title: The Beacon Everyone Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Months later, the beacon is a monument and schoolchildren visit it; Wren, now its junior keeper, teaches the new dream—the crew's names spoken aloud each night. Emotional beat: inheritance; memory kept deliberately rather than smuggled secretly.

chapters.title: Signal Forward
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Closing chapter: Sable outfits her freighter for a new run—not contraband this time, but copies of the archive bound for other colonies that received the Deep Rising's last silent broadcast. Emotional beat: hopeful departure; loyalty to truth carried outward, one honest delivery at a time.
